newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Defying speculation, the peso performed better than expected yesterday as it held at 29 pesos to the dollar on the first day of trading after the government allowed it to float last Friday. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- President Ramos has mobilised the various price monitoring councils under the Department of Trade and Industry to track the prices of commodities and stop unscrupulous traders from taking advantage of the peso depreciation. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Defence Secretary Renato de Villa told the Moro Islamic Liberation Front yesterday to drop any precondition for the resumption of stalled peace meetings with the government, saying such demands only slow the process. (STAR/STANDARD)

- Monetary authorities are prepared to further jack up its interest rates to cushion the possible impact of the change in peso-dollar rates, central bank governor Gabriel Singson told reporters yesterday. (CHRONICLE/STAR/TODAY)
- Banks speculating heavily on the exchange rate may be placed in hot water following the monetary authorities' decision to look into their dollar holdings. (CHRONICLE/BUSINESSWORLD/BULLETIN)
- Treasury bill rates yesterday surged across the board, but all the three maturities were undersubscribed. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
